issue: Confirmed zero LNG terminals/candidates for Bosnia and Herzegovina. Bosnia's only Adriatic coastline access is the ~20km stretch at Neum, which is a tender/cruise port with no freight or deepwater cargo infrastructure (development plans exist but face local opposition over the Bay of Mali Ston/Neum's ecotourism economy) and no LNG-specific proposal was found for it. The only current LNG-adjacent development for Bosnia is the 'Southern Interconnection' (Južna interkonekcija), a ~160km NATURAL GAS PIPELINE project (Croatia border segment ~60km + BiH segment ~120km, US firm AAFS Infrastructure and Energy named as investor, April 2026 agreement) that would connect Bosnia's gas grid to Croatia's Krk FSRU terminal by pipeline to diversify away from Russian gas. This is a pipeline interconnector, not a marine LNG import/export terminal, so it is out of scope for this tracker regardless of its LNG linkage — no Bosnian-soil terminal, storage, or regas facility is involved.
suggested_action: No staging. Re-check only if Neum's cargo-port redevelopment plans firm up with an explicit LNG/regas component, or if a distinct marine terminal proposal emerges.
